# Māgaṇḍiya Sutta (Snp 4.9 (PTS Snp 163))

**ID:** Snp 4.9 (PTS Snp 163)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Māgaṇḍiya Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Māgaṇḍiya Sutta* is the ninth discourse of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* [Norman 1997-2001; Hazra 1994]. In this discourse, the wanderer Māgaṇḍiya offers his daughter in marriage to the Buddha, who rejects the offer and subdues Māgaṇḍiya's pride by expounding an inward peace that transcends sensual desires, dogmatic views, and conceptual entanglements. The text stresses freedom from notions and dogmas: for one devoid of perceptions there are no bonds, and for one liberated by wisdom there are no delusions, whereas those clinging to perception and views continually clash with others in the world [Wen].

The discourse is one of the earliest securely attested pieces of the Pali canon. In the *Hāliddikānisutta* (SN 22.3; S III 9), verse 844 of this sutta is explicitly cited as the *Aṭṭhaka-vaggika Māgaṇḍiya-pañha* and expounded by the elder Mahākaccāna [Norman 1997-2001; Hazra 1994]. This early canonical exegesis is closely connected with the development of the *Niddesa* tradition, where the entire sutta is systematically analyzed in the canonical commentary *Māgaṇḍiyasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 9) [Hazra 1994; DharmaNexus].
